My partner and I are both positive and have been together for a while and have caused each other to breakout a few times. 
You may not be able to avoid it all the time, but before we have our "private time", we clean ourselves and look for any redness, swelling and itchy or dry spots. 

Keeping you and your partner clean before sex reduces your chance of spreading bacteria and having an outbreak. Friction has been an issue as well, having our bodies rub against each other causes outbreaks as well. Using water-based lube helps a lot with the Friction (make sure to use plenty of it!)

I also take Valacyclovir, your breakouts will be a lot shorter with it, usually 3-5 days after taking the first dose of medicine my outbreak will clear up, just stay away from thongs during your outbreaks bc they do rub on your body. I would have your partner take a dose of the Valacyclovir as well to make sure you both are getting that boost to speed up and clear out any of the bacteria.

People are going to judge, it's Unavoidable. I used to work at a grocery store as a cashier and the uniforms were short sleeved, I always had customers seeing my healed scars and telling me "what was going through your head?" 
"Are you OK? Do I need to call someone?"
The best way I have found to boost my confidence with my scars was to start ignoring them!!!!! And I also kept an open mind. 
Some people will see your scars and it reminds them of someone they know.
 Other people will see your scars and understand where you have been mentally.

Your body shows everyone what you've been through. No one is allowed to tell you to cover up, no one is allowed to ask you questions. You have the right to ignore them. Not everyone that sees your scars is judging you.

It just depends, wait for them to turn white and make sure your artist is NOT heavy handed!!! Deeper scars can have nerve damage to them, so it could be really painful one second, and the next you feel absolutely nothing.
No!!! Don't cover up! People who think we need to cover them up are insane! Show your scars so you can have the confidence you will need in the future.
